PullRequest.Title: sessions: prototype Customizations-style Automations
PullRequest.Body:
This opt-in Automations prototype uses the Customizations layout: a compact header, contextual filters, a dense table and a resizable details panel. Opening an automation makes room for its details instead of covering the list, so you can keep searching and switching between automations.

The layout now reuses the current run-history surface, native creation and editing forms, blueprint import/drop handling and cloud View options. Off automations stay in their ownership sections, sorted after those that are on, with a remembered **Show turned-off automations** choice. Off and provider unavailable remain separate states.

### Try it

Open the Agents window with:

```json
{
  "chat.automations.enabled": true,
  "chat.automations.layout": "modal",
  "chat.automations.sampleData": false
}
```

Use a connected automation provider for live actions. Select a row, resize its details panel, change the workspace/location/status filters, and use Escape to return to the row. The native **Create with Agent** split button keeps **Create Manually** and **Import Automation...** in its dropdown.

Create or edit an automation, turn it off and back on, duplicate it, or export and re-import its blueprint. Open a run's exact session and artifacts, then use **Manage runs** for that automation's history. The shared history keeps read/unread, rename, done/restore, Sessions-list visibility and retained-history deletion actions. Scoped **Mark all as read** affects only the displayed automation.

For a read-only visual preview, set `"chat.automations.sampleData": true`. Those examples and results are labeled sample data; they do not execute or open real sessions.

### Scope

This draft includes current Microsoft main through `06bea887795` and supersedes the closed comparison in `eli-w-king/eli-vscode#10`. The default `page` layout remains the baseline, and the experimental `chatInput` variant is retained. Agent creation uses the upstream action and its draft-replacement confirmation.

The modal editor is registered by the ordinary desktop/web entry. The isolated mobile package keeps its existing page when the modal setting is synced to it.

Live results use existing provider/session metadata. There is no new summary backend, scheduling policy or deletion policy. Cloud ownership, event and tool configuration use the existing form and provider contracts. An isolated scripted-provider walkthrough is not evidence of live GitHub backend execution.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Traced the unconditional runs.map, both getSession calls, and SessionsManagementService.getSession through _getAllSessions and provider.getAllSessions. The latter rebuilds session arrays even with warm provider caches. The existing view's single snapshot/map provides a direct before/after comparison. Duration depends on history and session counts, not on an uncertain call path.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repeated allocation of complete provider/session arrays and linear URI/previous-identity comparisons.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For H linked visible history runs and S known sessions, the runs projection makes about 2H full-collection lookups: O(H*S) work and array-element allocation per recomputation. Marking U distinct sessions read can cause U recomputations because those observable writes are not batched together. Warm session caches do not eliminate array reconstruction.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased opening/update latency and renderer CPU/GC pressure; bulk read-state changes multiply the synchronous work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing cards/history surface took one getSessions snapshot, indexed it by URI comparison key, and associated history through map lookups, O(S+H) for this association. Its history rendering is also suspended while Mark all as read is running; ordinary already-presented runs do not require the cards' fallback session lookups.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Opening either experimental layout now resolves every linked historical run through a collection-wide session lookup, and repeats these lookups whenever the runs projection is invalidated, including individual read-state changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new history projection calls getSession for every run at automationsLayoutWidget.ts:568, after withLocalProgress already calls it at :546. The existing AutomationsCardsWidget instead builds sessionsByResource once at automationsView.ts:336-348 and passes that map into history rendering.
Findings.Title: Index sessions once before projecting run history
Findings.Impact: With hundreds of retained runs and a large session history, opening Automations or processing live session updates performs repeated full-session scans on the renderer thread. Mark all as read is particularly costly: individual isRead changes rerun the whole projection despite the provider's event batching, potentially freezing the surface and generating substantial garbage.
Findings.Evidence: AutomationsLayoutModel.runs maps the entire visible history at lines 564-598; each linked run invokes getSession through withLocalProgress and again at line 568. SessionsManagementService.getSession (sessionsManagementService.ts:435-445) calls _getAllSessions(), which enumerates every provider's sessions, then performs a linear find. BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getAllSessions (:5608-5641) constructs a fresh array on every call. The widget unconditionally observes model.runs at :1032, even outside Runs/details. The projection also observes each finished session's isRead at :590; setSessionsReadState (:8397-8406) pauses provider events but does not transactionally batch those observable changes.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve sessions from one URI-identity-aware snapshot/index per model update instead of calling getSession inside the run loop and its progress helper. Preserve hidden-session and previous-identity resolution semantics, and coalesce the projection during bulk read updates.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The observable subscriptions and unconditional destructive render calls are explicit. Agent-host activity updates reach session.description and session-change notifications, and the model subscribes to both. The old view's persistentCards and identity-checked history blocks establish that full reconstruction is new. No timing measurements are assumed.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, Button/Switch instances, hover registrations, event listeners, and browser layout work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each observed run/session update recreates O(N) expanded, filtered automation rows and, when details are open, O(Ha) run-detail rows for that automation. Cost grows with update frequency times N+Ha; there is no scheduling/coalescing before these synchronous renders. Collapsed sections reduce N but do not prevent rebuilding the remaining table.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated renderer CPU work, DOM/control allocation and garbage collection, increasing the risk of dropped frames during live updates.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The baseline page retained keyed automation cards and persistent history groups/session lists. Live session presentation could update its own observable consumers without disposing and reconstructing the complete automation catalogue; unchanged session-list membership short-circuited updates.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: An individual run's activity, title, artifacts, or read-state update now tears down and recreates the entire displayed automation table, plus the selected automation's entire run-details body when open.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new widget autorun at :1027-1051 reads the complete model.runs and always calls renderPane. Added lines :1536-1540 clear all row disposables, switches, and DOM before rebuilding every displayed row. The open-details autorun similarly rebuilds its complete body at :2196-2217.
Findings.Title: Preserve table rows across live run updates
Findings.Impact: While an automation is running, activity updates repeatedly reconstruct even unrelated rows. With a substantial automation list or long history in the open details panel, this causes avoidable main-thread allocation/layout work and visible interaction or scrolling jank. Updating another automation's run also rebuilds the selected details.
Findings.Evidence: The widget subscribes to model.runs regardless of selected navigation (:1032). That model reads live session outcomes, artifacts, changes, and read state (:582-590), so changes unrelated to a table row's displayed fields still invalidate the table. renderPane disposes all controls and clears this.content (:1536-1540), then renderAutomationSections/renderAutomationRow recreate all shown rows, Buttons, Switches, hovers, and listeners. Details also subscribe to the global runs collection (:2085-2088), clear their body (:2196-2198), and map every own run into new DOM (:2306). In contrast, AutomationCardsSection keeps persistentCards (:642-651), and AutomationHistorySection.updateGroupSessions (:2338-2344) returns when session identities are unchanged.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep keyed row/control instances and update only changed presentation fields. Separate navigation counts and live run-detail dependencies from the catalogue renderer, and scope details updates to the selected automation rather than the global runs collection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup, default page layout, switching layouts, and closing the modal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration happens during sessions startup; the large new widget/model is constructed on demand for modal/chatInput. Layout reconciliation is queued. Normal modal closure disposes the editor part and widget, and changing custom-view layouts disposes the previous widget.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open Automations surfaces and explicit layout changes, not session-history cardinality until a widget is instantiated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Layout reconciliation uses a Sequencer; queued work reads the current layout. Widget timers stop on disposal. No independently retained modal/background widget was established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The page layout remains the default. No new persistent session cache or negative-cache behavior is introduced by registration. Model subscriptions, timers, and controls are owned by disposable stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in on-demand construction and disposal, based on the layout contribution, modal editor ownership, and custom-view autorun stores.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup parsing cost of the new imports is unmeasured; no concrete scaling or critical-path regression was established from module size alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup or cleanup-lifecycle finding. Default-page behavior is substantially retained; the reported regressions affect the new layout instances.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Automations and refreshing cloud definitions/history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The surface first projects cached in-memory data synchronously. An asynchronous initial refresh and subsequent completion-spaced 60-second refreshes update it later; remote discovery is not awaited before initial paint. Fresh cloud results require account initialization, repository discovery, definition refresh, then history refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve local workspace GitHub remotes by finding .git and reading git config, including worktree indirection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential resolution per recent local workspace root, before repository-key deduplication; up to 50 parent .git stat attempts per root, a config read when found, and optional .git/commondir reads. Virtual GitHub roots need no local Git-config read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing cards already refreshed the same stores immediately and periodically through this resolver; no new Git subprocess was found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes configuration and definition refresh, but runs after the first cached UI projection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward cloud API operation envelopes and serialized request/response bodies through the existing remote API provider where the shared-process client is used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request forwarding per API operation/page before transport coalescing, with the same repository/definition/history cardinality as before. No forwarding is performed merely to render an individual run's cached metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same account-client/store calls already crossed this boundary from the page layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of asynchronous cloud refresh, not initial local projection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read repository configuration, paginated definition summaries/full definitions, recent automation tasks, and active-task details using the existing Mission Control APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration operation per unique repository; eligible repositories list definitions in pages of 100 capped at ten pages, followed by one full-definition read per summary in batches of five. One listRuns operation per included definition returns the first 50 tasks; only active tasks receive detail reads. Identical concurrent GETs can coalesce; warm GETs can revalidate through ETags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old cards surface performed the same grouped, serialized/limited refresh. The diff changes presentation, not per-run remote request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks publication of refreshed remote snapshots, while cached content can already be shown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: W recent workspace roots before repository grouping; R unique repositories after persisted/target/recent deduplication; D definitions across eligible repositories; at most 50 recent unarchived runs returned per included cloud definition, plus active-task detail reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ProviderAutomationService.refresh uses Promise.all across provider stores. GitHub store operations share a Sequencer. Recent workspace resolution and repositories are traversed serially; definition details are fetched in batches of five; history has Limiter(4), with active task details serial within each worker. The unchanged transport additionally has bounded queue admission (defaults: 12 total/host, 10 account, 8 caller), priorities, and rate-limit delays.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider snapshots and the account client are reused; initial/refresh promises coalesce in flight. Cloud GET requests retain the existing transport's in-flight coalescing and ETag revalidation, so warm bodies can avoid transfer but do not imply zero request/revalidation work. Repository config resolution itself has no new widget cache; cloud capability cooldown behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in refresh placement, grouping, limiter, sequencer, request forwarding, and warm revalidation from the traced implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository count, active-task count, network latency, and ETag hit rate vary. None is needed to establish the separately reported local projection/render regressions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No newly introduced network fan-out finding. Opening the new layouts nevertheless incurs the reported repeated session-enumeration CPU work before the asynchronous refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live session/run changes while the automation list or details panel is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session notifications update cached provider observables; the new model synchronously projects all visible historical runs, and widget autoruns synchronously render the catalogue and any open details body before the renderer can process further interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive existing agent-host session status/activity/title/change notifications and apply them to cached session models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing notification cadence, including streamed status/activity updates. The diff adds local subscribers and processing, not a new outgoing call per run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notifications updated persistent cards/history/session renderers without rebuilding every automation control.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notification processing now reaches the new all-history projection and destructive UI render on the renderer thread.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H visible linked historical runs, S known sessions across providers, N displayed expanded/filtered automation rows, Ha selected-automation history rows, and F live invalidations. Hundreds of retained runs/sessions are sufficient to make the new multiplicative work significant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CPU projection and DOM reconstruction run synchronously in renderer autoruns, not in a worker or bounded asynchronous queue. Observable transactions can combine their contained writes, but subsequent activity events still invalidate the whole runs collection. No UI render coalescing is present on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getSession checks unlisted drafts first, but ordinary published historical sessions call _getAllSessions and allocate provider/session arrays on every lookup, even when provider data is warm. The new table/details renderer does not retain keyed row instances across model invalidations. Artifacts, changes, and activity descriptions inspected here are cached observable projections, not independently proven remote hydration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: two lookups per linked history row trace directly to full provider enumeration; broad observable subscriptions trace directly to clear/dispose/recreate calls. These mechanisms do not rely on new remote reads or a cold cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Update cadence and displayed collection sizes are workload-dependent; frame times and allocations were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two findings submitted: O(H*S) session association per projection, and independent O(N+Ha) DOM/control reconstruction per observed update. Both are introduced by the new layouts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search, navigation, opening details, scrolling, and resize
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Query/navigation/filter changes synchronously re-render the active pane. The existing history section is instantiated lazily on the first Runs selection. Opening details derives selected content and creates its history DOM; split-view/resize work runs synchronously. Scrolling uses the existing scrollable elements.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation rows surviving the filter/collapsed sections; full run collection used for counts/scoping; all selected-automation runs in details. Hidden history is retained after its first use, but within the widget's disposed lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer-thread autoruns and split-view layout are synchronous. History subscriptions remain active after first visit when its host is hidden; no separate asynchronous worker or request per filtered row was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search and metadata reads are local. A lazily created history widget is reused on later tab visits. Details rows are rebuilt, not cached, and there is no paging cap in the new details run list. Composer ResizeObserver checks previous dimensions before relayout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that these presentation operations do not trigger metadata network hydration; cached provider derivations and the render methods were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical automation/history sizes and input cadence are unknown; no independent forced-layout duration was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Broad invalidation/reconstruction is covered by the rendering finding, not duplicated as separate search, hidden-history, or layout findings. No separate high-confidence forced-layout mechanism was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark one run or scoped/all completed runs read
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing helper computes completed unread sessions from one session snapshot, deduplicates by URI comparison key, and awaits sessionsManagementService.markAllRead. The new runs model directly observes each finished session's isRead, so its projection can execute synchronously during individual state changes before the action completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist existing session/chat read-state changes through provider dispatch to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Provider API grouping is P calls, but dispatch still depends on the U distinct sessions and their unread chats; no new per-history-row persistence call is introduced. Providers that do not need remote persistence remain local.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper/provider operations persisted read states, with provider event grouping. The baseline history suppressed refresh during the bulk action and associated sessions through a single snapshot/map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits provider work; local isRead publication can additionally trigger the newly introduced synchronous projection/render work while the action is running.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U distinct unread completed sessions after URI deduplication, grouped into P providers; provider-specific unread chat count; H visible linked historical runs and S known sessions for each invalidated projection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: markAllRead groups sessions by provider and calls providers with Promise.all. Agent-host setSessionsReadState pauses/merges its onDidChangeSessions emitter but calls individual setSessionReadState operations concurrently; it does not place all isRead observable writes in one transaction. Other providers can use the fallback per-session Promise.all. The old history has an isMarkingAllRead gate; the new model/table do not share that suspension.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Read-state operations reuse cached session models; provider change-event batching does not cache or suppress the new model's direct observable reads. No new negative cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the model reads individual isRead observables, and pausing the provider emitter is distinct from batching observable transactions. URI deduplication and provider grouping were explicitly accounted for.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of unread sessions and provider/chat mix vary; the multiplicative local cost is established without assuming a particular IPC duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: A particularly strong trigger for the submitted repeated-session-enumeration finding: up to U projection invalidations, each O(H*S), despite grouped provider notifications. No separate new IPC fan-out finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create/edit/toggle/run/cancel automations, import/export blueprints, and prepare ChatInput authoring requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: User-initiated persistence awaits existing dialog/service/provider commits and acknowledgement. Run now invokes the existing runner for one chosen automation. Import reads/parses one accepted blueprint before review; export writes one selected file. ChatInput's new request preparation awaits the shared skill-discovery result before forwarding the authoring request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch existing catalogue mutations or one runAutomation request and wait for authoritative provider state/response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected automation operation, with existing provider validation and acknowledgement; not one operation per displayed run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing page/dialog/runner actions used the same provider contracts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the explicit mutation/run result, not initial list rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute existing cloud automation CRUD/dispatch API requests and authoritative preflights/reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Selected automation only, with unchanged store preflights and serialization; no collection-wide mutation request loop added by the layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands and service methods already performed these mutations from the page layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the requested cloud mutation; not a new render-time operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one accepted dropped/selected blueprint via fileService.readFile or browser File.arrayBuffer; serialize and write one exported blueprint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One accepted file read per import/drop and one write per confirmed export; parsing/serialization scales with that file's bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extracted shared drop/import/export paths retain the existing read-parse-review-create and serialize-write behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Import review waits for read/parse; export completion waits for write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The new ChatInput preparation asks existing cached discovery for the built-in automation skill; a cold/invalidated discovery can locate and parse skill files through existing file reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero additional discovery reads for a warm cache; one shared discovery computation across concurrent callers on a miss, including the discovered K skills, rather than K reads per request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new custom authoring surface did not exist; skill discovery and its shared cache already served the normal chat/prompt infrastructure. No duplication of cold discovery or cache bypass was established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added preparatory await is before authoring-request forwarding; cold discovery latency can be visible, whereas warm calls reuse the cached promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One automation per mutation/run action; independent automation IDs for simultaneous toggles; one accepted blueprint file and its byte size; K discovered skill files on an invalidated/cold skill-discovery cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Different automation toggles are not globally serialized by the widget; the cloud store retains its operation sequencer. Agent-host mutations dispatch one catalogue request and observe acknowledgement; runAutomation issues one selected automation request unless already active. Inline editor cleanup waits for any active commit. Cold skill discovery combines sources, then parses discovered skills sequentially; concurrent callers share its promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: pendingToggles prevents duplicate concurrent saves for the same automation. Provider catalogues and cloud account/store caches are reused. Skill discovery uses one CachedPromise, sharing in-flight work and warm results; skill/model/extension/bundled/plugin-related invalidations or failures can cause recomputation. No evidence supports a full filesystem skill scan on every warm request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in command reuse, per-ID save guards, shared discovery, and explicit filesystem/provider calls from the traced implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File sizes, cold skill counts, and provider/network latency vary. The cold authoring dependency is intentional and bounded by existing shared discovery; no independent redundant-work regression was proven there.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance findings: existing mutation/file boundaries are reused without new collection fan-out, and warm skill requests do not rescan files.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a selected automation run in a session or external browser
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new action forwards exactly the selected resource to the existing session-opening service, or external opener as fallback. Session opening resolves resource identity, mounts the session/loading UI, prepares/reopens the selected session, then waits for load; a newer navigation can cancel the earlier open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing provider-backed session resolution/preparation/open path for one chosen run, or invoke the external opener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected resource; downstream cold load depends on that provider/session. Already-open sessions can be revealed without loading another session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing automation/history surfaces already opened a chosen session or external run using the same session/opener infrastructure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session preparation/load follows mounting of existing loading UI and is required only for this explicit open action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected session or external URI per click, independent of the number of history rows displayed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing navigation cancellation and session-open lifecycle are retained. For a selected session, reopen and prepare work can run in Promise.all after mounting; no loop opens all history entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing session identity/cache/model and already-open host reuse apply. Reading run metadata beforehand does not eagerly open/hydrate every run.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in single-resource forwarding and unchanged service navigation/preparation flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider session load may be slow, but its duration and backend behavior are unchanged by this forwarding action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression from richer run metadata or open-run forwarding alone.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 31 changed files and all diff pages against base 06bea887795fc42064969eb06b524ad0d02f2781. Submitted two medium-severity, high-confidence regressions in the new Automations layouts: repeated full-session enumeration for every history row, and destructive catalogue/details reconstruction on broad live updates. Accounted for repository/session deduplication, warm/in-flight caches, provider event batching versus observable writes, cloud sequencing/limiters, asynchronous refresh placement, and disposal. No qualifying regression fix/provenance signal identified. Review is static; costs and frame times are unmeasured. The supporting guide tool returned only a preview because its output exceeded the tool limit; embedded skill guidance and learned-regression guidance were available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
